security_audit.summary: All 59 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, or placeholder credential variables. Two semantic concerns remain: the production example enables local authentication, and the deletion example lacks confirmation guidance.

remediation.issue: The production workspace example enables local authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Disable local authentication by default and explain when an exception is justified.

remediation.issue: The deletion example lacks target verification and confirmation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation and display the subscription, resource group, and workspace before deletion.

semantic_findings.title: Local Authentication Enabled in Production Example
semantic_findings.description: The production-tagged workspace example enables local authentication, allowing access-token authentication instead of an identity-only posture.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly sets LocalAuth to Enabled and tags the resource as Production. This is clear guidance that can weaken authentication controls.

semantic_findings.title: Workspace Deletion Lacks Confirmation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill provides a completed Azure workspace deletion operation without requiring target verification or explicit user confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented call waits for deletion to complete, and the surrounding guidance contains no confirmation or resource identity safeguard.

content.value_statement: Managing Microsoft Playwright Testing resources requires precise Azure SDK calls and lifecycle handling. This skill provides focused .NET guidance for common management operations.
actual_capabilities: Explains package installation and Azure authentication with DefaultAzureCredential.
Shows how to create, retrieve, list, update, and delete Playwright Testing workspaces.
Demonstrates subscription and workspace quota queries.
Provides a name availability check workflow.
Maps core SDK resource types and workspace properties.
Connects the management-plane workspace URI to Playwright test execution configuration.
limitations: Covers management-plane resources, not complete Playwright test authoring or execution.
Requires an existing Azure subscription, permissions, resource group, and local .NET environment.
Examples use fixed names and regions that must be adapted and validated.
Does not provide deployment templates, cost estimates, or production policy enforcement.

use_cases.title: Provision a Test Workspace
use_cases.description: Create a Playwright Testing workspace with selected region, tags, and authentication settings.

use_cases.title: Audit Workspace Capacity
use_cases.description: List workspaces and inspect subscription or workspace quota before scaling test execution.

use_cases.title: Automate Resource Lifecycle
use_cases.description: Build idempotent .NET routines for updates, error handling, and controlled workspace removal.

prompt_templates.title: Install the SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the packages and prerequisites for using Azure.ResourceManager.Playwright in a new .NET project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a .NET workflow to create a Playwright Testing workspace in [region] and resource group [name]. Use DefaultAzureCredential.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Existing Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET routine that lists Playwright workspaces, reports provisioning state, and checks subscription and workspace quotas.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Controlled Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an idempotent .NET workspace lifecycle with validation, error handling, secure authentication, update logic, and confirmed deletion.

output_examples.input: Create a production workspace in West US 3.
output: Prerequisites: authenticated Azure identity, subscription identifier, resource group, and required role.
Plan: validate the target, disable local authentication by default, apply production tags, and wait for provisioning.
Result checks: confirm provisioning state, workspace identifier, and data-plane URI.

output_examples.input: Review quota before increasing cloud test usage.
output_examples.output: The response identifies subscription and workspace quota queries, compares limits with usage, and highlights capacity requiring review.
The response first displays the subscription, resource group, and workspace, requests explicit confirmation, then verifies completed deletion.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and grant only the Azure roles required for each operation.
Validate subscription, resource group, workspace name, and region before any mutation.
Handle RequestFailedException and verify the final provisioning state of long-running operations.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode service principal secrets or access tokens in source files.
Do not enable local authentication without a documented operational requirement.
Do not delete a workspace without explicit confirmation and target verification.

faq.question: Does this skill run Playwright tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Azure management-plane operations for Playwright Testing workspaces.

faq.question: Which authentication method does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends DefaultAzureCredential, which can use local developer credentials, managed identity, or configured service principal credentials.

faq.question: Can it create and update workspaces?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents workspace creation, retrieval, listing, tag updates, and related long-running operation handling.

faq.question: Can it inspect quota?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers subscription-level and workspace-level quota queries.

faq.question: Does it support safe deletion?
faq.answer: It shows the deletion API. Production use should add explicit confirmation, target verification, and post-deletion checks.

faq.question: What must I provide before using the examples?
faq.answer: Provide the Azure subscription, resource group, workspace name, region, permissions, and authentication context.
